pairs: Canticum graduum.
A Canticle in steps.
Beati omnes qui timent Dominum,
Blessed are all those who fear the Lord,
qui ambulant in viis ejus.
who walk in his ways.
Labores manuum tuarum quia manducabis:
For you will eat by the labors of your hands.
beatus es,
Blessed are you,
et bene tibi erit.
and it will be well with you.
Uxor tua sicut vitis abundans in lateribus domus tuæ;
Your wife is like an abundant vine on the sides of your house.
filii tui sicut novellæ olivarum in circuitu mensæ tuæ.
Your sons are like young olive trees surrounding your table.
Ecce sic benedicetur homo qui timet Dominum.
Behold, so will the man be blessed who fears the Lord.
Benedicat tibi Dominus ex Sion,
May the Lord bless you from Zion,
et videas bona Jerusalem omnibus diebus vitæ tuæ.
and may you see the good things of Jerusalem, all the days of your life.
Et videas filios filiorum tuorum:
And may you see the sons of your sons.
pacem super Israël.
Peace be upon Israel.
